chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The least amount that suffices from the camphor for the deceased is one misqal.
And in the narration of Al-Kahili and Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: The moderate amount from that is four misqals.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ مَثَاقِيلَ: Four misqals, indicating the moderate or standard quantity
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: Camphor, a fragrant substance used in the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مِثْقَالٌ: A misqal, a unit of weight (approx. 4.7 grams)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of camphor required for washing the deceased in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the fiqh of ritual washing (ghusl al-mayyit) by establishing one misqal as the minimum sufficient quantity of camphor, while citing the narration of al-Kahili and Husayn ibn al-Mukhtār to identify four misqals as the preferred moderate amount (qasd). This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly methodology of balancing the legal minimum (kifāyah) with the recommended excellence (mustahabb) in funeral rites, ensuring the body is properly prepared for burial in accordance with the Imams' teachings.
